info.title: Eidola API
info.description: Privacy-transparent AI proxy API with inline verification metadata

post.description:
Accepts any active Stripe price ID. Automatically determines whether to
create a subscription or one-time payment checkout based on the price type.
For subscription prices, enforces the one-active-subscription constraint.

Idempotent per `(account, idempotency_key)`: the first request debits and
stores the signed response in one transaction, and a retry with the same
key and request is answered from what was stored, so a response lost on the
way back costs nothing. A stored issuance is answered before the terms gate
and the current-key check, because it was already paid for. A key that is
not current is refused with `409` only once the database, under the account
lock, has it no longer issuing, so no attempt under the idempotency key can
debit afterwards; otherwise `503`.

200.description: Credential issued, or the stored response to an earlier attempt under the same idempotency key

409.description: The idempotency key was used for a different request, the named issuer key has stopped issuing, or the account is closing or closed; no new debit can occur under this key

503.description: Credential issuance not configured, or the named issuer key is not yet this gateway's current issuing key; try again

post.summary:
POST /v1/account/portal — mint a Stripe billing-portal session
(authenticated).
post.description:
Separate from the subscription read on purpose. Minting is a write to
Stripe and the session expires quickly, so a link that rides a status
response is one no client can responsibly hold — ours already discarded
it and asked again at the moment of the click. Riding along, it made
every status read create-and-throw-away a Stripe session, and put that
write's latency in front of an answer that did not need it.

Refuses for an account with no payment relationship, on the same test
`GET /v1/account/subscription` calls `none`: a portal minted for someone
money has never moved for is a door onto an empty room.

get.summary: Read this account's durable repair status without initiating provider work.

post.summary:
Durably request billing reconciliation for the authenticated account.
An independent billing worker performs the provider calls. This remains
available without Stripe credentials, while reviewing terms and after
account closure. Poll GET on this path for completion and review items.

202.description: Repair request recorded; poll GET for its completed generation

400.description: Repair does not accept a request body

get.description:
Always 200 on a reachable Stripe: having no subscription is an answer,
not a failure. The states are distinguished so a client can tell "never
transacted" from "has a payment relationship but nothing in force" —
the second has a billing portal worth offering, the first does not.

post.summary:
POST /v1/account/terms — record acceptance of a current document version
(authenticated).

post.description:
Paid with one or two ACT (Anonymous Credit Token) spends in the body's
`credentials` member. Every spend proof is verified, every nullifier is
recorded, all or none, each with a provisional refund of nothing, and when
the request ends each is replaced by its input's final refund: the charge
is consumed in input order, and each input's unspent credits return under
its own issuer key.

`model` is `tag`, `tag@sha256:<hex>` or `sha256:<hex>` (a full SHA-256 in
lowercase hex), resolved to the model's weights hash before anything else.
A digest, when present, decides alone; a bare tag resolves through this
build's catalog. The response's `model` is `tag@sha256:<hex>` (or
`sha256:<hex>` for a hash named alone).

200.description: Chat completion response with privacy and verification metadata

400.description: Invalid request; a malformed model reference (`invalid_model_reference`: not `tag`, `tag@sha256:<hex>` or `sha256:<hex>`), a malformed refund recovery key, more than two credentials, one credential presented twice, a share of zero, or a credential in a header (refused before any credential is spent); or a hold above the worst-case cost (refunded in full)

402.description: A hold below the worst-case cost (refunded in full)

404.description: The model reference names no model (`model_not_found`); refunded in full

409.description: A credential already spent; none of the request's credentials is recorded

410.description: The model reference names a retired model (`model_retired`); refunded in full

503.description: No upstream is available for the model

post.summary: Recover a refund token for a previously spent ACT.
post.description:
If the ACT's nullifier was already recorded (the server received the
original request), the refund stored with it is returned: the final one
if the request has ended, or the provisional one (`t = 0`, marked
`provisional`) if it is still being served.

If the nullifier was NOT recorded (the original request never arrived),
the server verifies the spend proof, records the nullifier with a full
refund (no credits consumed) stored beside it, and returns that refund.

In both cases, the client gets a refund token it can combine with its
local `PreRefund` state to reconstruct a credential.

The stored token is sealed under the refund recovery key the client sent
with the spend, so recovery must present the same key: a different one
opens nothing and is answered as no token stored (404).

400.description: A malformed refund recovery key, more than one credential, or a credential in a header

401.description: Missing credential, or an invalid spend proof

404.description: Nullifier found but no refund token is available for this key

get.description:
One entry per weights hash, with its tags, source, per-file manifest,
lifecycle and the engine deployments that serve it (`docs/model-identity.md`).

get.summary: GET /v1/terms — the document versions whose acceptance is required.
get.description:
Public, and necessarily so: a client fetches this *before* it has an
account, to learn what it must accept. It takes no credential and returns
no account-specific data. (Accepting them is `POST /v1/account/terms`,
which is on the linked surface.)

AcceptTermsRequest.description: Acceptance of one currently required document version.

sha256.description:
Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the document text being accepted; must match
the currently required version from `GET /v1/terms`.

AssistantMessage.description: An assistant message in a response.

reasoning_content.description:
Reasoning ("thinking") output from models that emit it. Two
spellings are in the wild: OpenAI o-series and many compatible
gateways use `reasoning_content`; vLLM uses `reasoning`. We
faithfully round-trip whichever the upstream sent so clients can
pick. Both stay `None` for non-thinking models.

tool_calls.description:
Tool calls the model asked for. Relayed to the client **verbatim**
(raw `Value`s) so the ids and any provider extension fields survive —
the client replays these objects unchanged on its follow-up request,
and a narrower struct here would silently drop what it doesn't model,
exactly the defect the `reasoning*` fields above were added to fix.

linkable.description: Whether this authorization method allows linking across requests.

BackendAttestation.description: Backend attestation from the inference provider.

provider.description: The provider that issued the attestation (e.g., "redpill").

signature.description: The ECDSA signature over the signed content.

signing_address.description: The signing address (e.g., Ethereum address for Phala/RedPill).

BalancePool.description: One balance pool: credits sharing an origin and expiration.

amount.description: Credits remaining in this pool (micro-USD denominated).

expires_at.description:
ISO-8601 instant at which these credits expire; absent for credits
that never expire.

source.description: Where the pool came from: `subscription`, `purchase`, or `other`.

BalancesResponse.description:
Credit balance breakdown. All amounts are credits, denominated in
micro-USD (1 credit = $0.000001).

debts.description: Unrecovered chargeback value, valued in the original payment currency.

purchases.description: Counts of current provider objects examined, not newly granted credits.

Capability.description:
One capability leaf.

An object rather than a bare boolean, so a capability can grow a sibling
key later — an effort ladder, a weights measurement — without a type change
breaking a client already deployed against this shape.

amount_minor.description:
Decimal minor currency units. Fractional units preserve exact purchase
valuation internally; this is not a demand for another payment.

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the chunk was created.

oneOf.description: Usage statistics (included in the final chunk by some providers).

add_generation_prompt.description:
Whether the prompt ends with the header of a new assistant turn. Omit
it, or send `false` with `continue_final_message` (vLLM's convention:
its default is `true`, and it refuses the two together).

cache_key.description:
The client's prefix-cache key: 32 bytes, base64url without padding
(`eidola_common::engine_protocol`). The engine scopes prefix-cache
reuse to requests carrying the same key; without one, nothing a
request computes is reused by any other.

**Secret, and never serialized.** It is held decoded in a
scrubbed-on-drop buffer, prints redacted, and `Serialize` skips it, so
no re-serialization of a request (the pricing walk's, say) can carry
it anywhere. The one writer is
`engine_trust::protocol::engine_request_body`.

oneOf.description:
Continue the final assistant message instead of answering it: the
prompt ends inside that message, so the model resumes exactly where it
stopped. `true` (or `"content"`) continues its `content`;
`"reasoning_content"` continues its `reasoning_content`, for a message
that stopped before any answer. The members and their meaning are
vLLM's and SGLang's, and the field name is `transformers`'
`apply_chat_template` argument; the rules are
`eidola_common::engine_protocol::check_continuation`.

credentials.description:
The anonymous credits paying for this request: one element per spend
(one, or two: a drain and a fill), each an ACT Token and its refund
recovery key (`eidola_common::spend_credentials`), in the order the
charge is consumed from them. Required; a request without it is
refused before anything is recorded, as is one that carries a
credential in a header instead.

**Secret, and never serialized**, like `cache_key`: it prints
redacted, `Serialize` skips it, and the body forwarded to an engine
leaves it out (`engine_trust::protocol::engine_request_body`).

max_completion_tokens.description: The maximum number of completion tokens to generate.

messages.description: A list of messages comprising the conversation.

model.description: ID of the model to use.

oneOf.description: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating.

Streaming options. The OpenAI-compatible field; we accept it for
API parity with clients that already set it (e.g. an SDK setting
`include_usage: true` to capture token counts in the final chunk).
Note: the server overrides `include_usage` to `true` for any
streaming request before forwarding upstream — usage is required
for accurate per-token refunds and isn't a client choice.

tool_choice.description:
How the model should choose among `tools` (`"none"` / `"auto"` /
`"required"`, or a `{"type":"function", …}` object). Opaque
pass-through for the same reason as [`Self::tools`].

tools.description:
Tool (function) definitions the model may call.

**Opaque pass-through.** Each entry is forwarded upstream verbatim:
the server never executes a tool and has no reason to understand the
JSON Schema inside `function.parameters`, while modelling it would
mean rejecting (via this struct's `deny_unknown_fields`) every
provider extension a client legitimately sends. Keeping the entries
as raw `Value`s is also what lets the pricing contract measure
exactly the bytes that go on the wire — see
`handlers::chargeable_prompt_tokens_for`.

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the completion was created.

continuable.description:
On a `length` ending from an Eidola engine: whether the reasoning and
content given out can be sent back as a continued final message
(`continue_final_message`) that renders exactly the text the model
generated. A client offers continuation only where it is `true`.

oneOf.description: The reason the model stopped generating.

ChunkChoice.description: A choice delta in a streaming chunk.

continuable.description:
On a `length` ending from an Eidola engine: whether the reasoning and
content given out can be sent back as a continued final message
(`continue_final_message`) that renders exactly the text the model
generated. A client offers continuation only where it is `true`.

delta.description: The delta (partial update) for this choice.

oneOf.description: The reason the model stopped generating (only in final chunk).

ChunkDelta.description: A delta update in a streaming response.

reasoning_content.description:
Reasoning ("thinking") deltas — same dual spelling as
`AssistantMessage`. Without these fields here, serde silently
drops the upstream `reasoning_content` / `reasoning` keys during
deserialization and the client only ever sees `delta.content`.
Round-trip whatever the upstream emits.

tool_calls.description:
Streamed tool-call deltas, relayed **verbatim** as raw `Value`s.

Nothing about a streamed tool call is guaranteed to arrive whole: the
id, the function name and the `arguments` string all arrive in
fragments keyed by the entry's `index`, and the client reassembles
them. The proxy therefore must not model, reorder, or normalize these
entries — including the streaming-only `index` framing key, which the
client's accumulator needs. Same rule as `reasoning*` above: a field
this struct does not name is dropped on re-serialization.

ContentPart.description: A content part within a multimodal message.

ContinueFinalMessage.description:
What `continue_final_message` may carry: a flag, or the name of the final
message's field to continue.

DataExposure.description: Describes a party's visibility into request/response data.

sees.description: What data this party can see (e.g., ["prompt", "response", "token_count"]).

created.description: Unix timestamp of when the completion was created.

model.description: The model that produced the completion.

privacy.description: Privacy metadata describing data exposure and authorization.

refunds.description: One refund per spend, in the order the request presented them.

EidolaStreamMetadata.description:
Metadata event sent as the final SSE event before [DONE] in streaming responses.

Clients identify this by checking `object == "eidola.chat.completion.metadata"`.
Standard OpenAI clients will ignore it.

id.description: The completion ID this metadata belongs to.

refunds.description: One refund per spend, in the order the request presented them.

EngineDeploymentPin.description: One engine deployment that serves a model.

config_sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the deployment's committed `tinfoil-config.yml`, lowercase
hex (on Intel TDX, its MRCONFIGID).

measurement.description:
The attestation measurement every connection to the deployment is
held to, in `tinfoil-verifier`'s pin shape.

ErrorResponse.description: An error response in OpenAI format, optionally including a refund token.

refunds.description:
One refund per spend, in the order the request presented them
(present when an error occurs after the spends' nullifiers were
recorded).

FinishReason.description: The reason the model stopped generating.

detail.description: Optional detail level for the image.

url.description: The URL of the image, or a base64-encoded data URI.

idempotency_key.description:
64 lowercase hex digits (32 random bytes) the client chose for this
issuance and kept before sending it. A retry under the same key and the
same request receives the response the first attempt was given, with no
second debit; the same key with any other request is refused (`409`).

issuer_key_id.description:
The issuer key the client expects to be signed under: the current
issuing key it read from `GET /v1/keys`. Refused (`409`) before any
debit when it is not the current key, so a credential is never paid for
under a key the client would not accept.

ledger_entry_id.description: The ledger entry ID for this issuance.

IssuerKeyResponse.description: A single issuer public key in the `GET /v1/keys` response.

domain_separator.description: Domain separator used for parameter generation.

public_key.description: Base64url-encoded CBOR public key (compressed Ristretto255 point).

oneOf.description:
The content of the message.

Nullable since tool calling: an assistant message that only called
tools carries `"content": null`. The key is deliberately **always
serialized** (no `skip_serializing_if`) — several chat templates
require it to exist, and clients send the explicit `null` for that
reason, so dropping it on the way upstream would change the request.

name.description: An optional name for the participant.

reasoning_content.description:
An assistant message's reasoning, which the model's chat template
renders before its content: what a continuation of a message that
stopped mid-reasoning carries, and charged as prompt text
(`eidola_common::prompt_charge`).

role.description: The role of the message author.

tool_call_id.description: The id of the tool call this message answers (`role: "tool"` only).

tool_calls.description:
Tool calls the assistant made, replayed by the client verbatim on the
follow-up request.

**Opaque pass-through**, like [`ChatCompletionRequest::tools`]: the
client is required to replay the provider's own call objects
unchanged (ids and any provider extension fields intact), so the
server must not normalize them through a narrower struct.

MessageContent.description: Message content can be a simple string or array of content parts (for multimodal).

Modality.description: A kind of content a model accepts or produces.

context_length.description: Maximum context window size in tokens.

deployments.description:
The engine deployments that serve these weights: each config's hash
and the attestation measurement this gateway holds it to.

description.description: Short description of the model's capabilities.

id.description:
The id to request the model by: its first tag, which follows the tag
(`tag`), or `sha256:<hex>` when it has none. A request may also name
`tag@sha256:<hex>` (the tag, asserted to resolve to this hash) or
`sha256:<hex>` (these weights, under any tag).

lifecycle.description: Whether the model is current or deprecated, and when it retires.

max_output_tokens.description:
The largest completion this model may be asked for.

Separate from `context_length` on purpose: a context window is what a
request may *contain*, not what one response may *be*. `null` means
undeclared — a client must treat that as "unknown" and keep whatever
default it already applies, never as zero.

output_budget_class.description: Which public output-budget ladder this model draws from.

pricing.description: Pricing in integer credits per 1k tokens.

sha256.description:
The model's identity: its weights hash, lowercase hex
(`docs/model-identity.md`).

tags.description: Every tag that resolves to this hash. Each tag names exactly one hash.

weights.description: Where the weights come from, and every file the hash covers.

ModelCapabilities.description:
What a model can do, as the catalog declares it.

Only axes that actually vary across the models this server sells are
carried. An axis every model shares tells a client nothing and is one more
assertion that has to stay true. `prompt_cache` and `pinned_weights` are
what each model's engine pin fixes.

input_modalities.description: The content kinds the model accepts.

output_modalities.description: The content kinds the model produces.

pinned_weights.description: The weights this gateway pins for the model, and where they came from.

prompt_cache.description:
Whether, and for how long, requests may reuse each other's prompt
prefix (`cache_key`).

reasoning.description: Whether the model produces reasoning content before its answer.

tool_calling.description:
Whether the model accepts a `tools` request field.

Named after the wire rather than after an adjective: the question a
client actually has is "will this request be accepted", and a field
name answers it where "supports tool use" does not.

ModelLifecycle.description: A model's place in its lifecycle.

retire_after.description: For a deprecated model, the announced retirement date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

status.description: `current` or `deprecated` (a retired model is not listed).

ModelPricing.description: Pricing for a model in scaled integer credits per token (or per request).

oneOf.description:
Per-request pricing (for models like Whisper or TTS that charge per request
rather than per token). When present, `per_prompt_token` and
`per_completion_token` are zero.

OutputBudgetClass.description:
Which public output-budget ladder a model draws from.

A *class*, not a number: the ladder's rungs are policy that can move
without the catalog moving, and keeping the selection public and
per-model is what keeps an output budget from becoming a per-user value.

PinnedWeightsCapability.description:
The exact weights a model is served from, when this gateway pins them.

`supported` means this gateway build accepts only deployments serving the
weights hashed here, and tells each one so on every request. `sha256` is
the engine's weights hash (a SHA-256 over the manifest of every file the
engine reads from its weights directory); `repo` and `revision` say where
those files were taken from. All three are absent when `supported` is
false.

supported.description: Whether the weights are pinned by this gateway.

PortalResponse.description:
A freshly minted Stripe billing-portal session.

Its own endpoint rather than a field on the subscription standing:
minting is a **write** to Stripe and the session expires quickly, so a
link handed out with a status read is one the client cannot responsibly
keep — and every status read was creating a portal session that was then
thrown away.

portal_url.description:
Open this in a browser now. Short-lived by construction; ask again
rather than storing it.

credits.description:
Credits granted by this plan, denominated in micro-USD
(1 credit = $0.000001). Subscription credits expire at the end of
each billing period; one-time purchase credits expire one year
after purchase.

unit_amount.description: Purchase price in the minor unit of `currency` (e.g. cents for USD).

PrivacyMetadata.description:
Privacy metadata describing how the request was authorized, what data is
visible to which parties, and transport security properties.

data_exposure.description: Which parties can see which data, and under what guarantees.

PromptCacheCapability.description:
Prompt-cache reuse across requests.

`supported` means requests to this model may carry a `cache_key`, and that
requests carrying the same key can reuse each other's computed prompt
prefix. The two bounds are the serving deployments' measured retention:
a prefix nothing has used for `idle_ttl_secs`, or any prefix older than
`max_age_secs`, is never reused and is zeroed. Both are absent when
`supported` is false.

idle_ttl_secs.description: Longest a cached prefix stays reusable without being used, in seconds.

max_age_secs.description: Longest a cached prefix stays reusable at all, in seconds.

ProxyAttestation.description: Proxy attestation (placeholder for future TEE deployment).

completed_generation.description:
Generation covered by `report`. While pending, this report describes
the last completed run, not the latest request.

last_error.description:
Fixed failure category from the last unsuccessful attempt, if any.
The durable request remains pending and may be retried by the worker.

requested_generation.description:
Latest durable repair request. A request arriving during a run remains
pending until a subsequent run covers its generation.

RefundInfo.description: A refund token issued after spending an ACT.

issuer_key_id.description: The issuer key ID that signed this refund.

RefundRecoveryRequest.description:
Body of the refund recovery endpoint: the spend to recover, in the same
`credentials` form it was presented in.

credentials.description: Exactly one spend: its Token and its refund recovery key.

RefundRecoveryResponse.description: Response from the refund recovery endpoint.

provisional.description:
Whether the refund is the provisional one stored when the spend was
recorded (`t = 0`) and its request is still being served, so it may
end with a larger one. A client keeps the spend pending and asks again,
since the final refund's successor shares its nullifier and spending
either destroys the other. `false` once the stored refund is the
spend's last word: a final refund, or a provisional one no request is
serving any more (a crash or a restart left it), which recovery then
rewrites as final, so no later write can change it.

refunds.description: The spend's refund: an array of one, mirroring `credentials`.

RequiredDocument.description:
A document whose current version must be accepted before purchases or
credential issuance. `sha256` identifies the exact text (the markdown
source, retrievable at `{url}source.md`), so acceptance binds to
precise words rather than a mutable URL; `version` is the document's
monotonically increasing front-matter version, which orders releases
(accepting version N satisfies any requirement ≤ N).

sha256.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 of the exact published document text.

url.description: Where the current text is published.

Role.description: The role of a message author.

ScaledPrice.description:
A price expressed as an integer value with a fixed scale factor.

Actual credits per unit = `value / scale_factor`.

SpendCredential.description: One element of a request body's `credentials` member, as documented.

refund_key.description:
The spend's refund recovery key: exactly 64 lowercase hex digits. The
stored copy of the spend's refund is sealed under it, and recovery
must present it again.

token.description:
One ACT Token (`token_type`, `challenge_digest`, `issuer_key_id`, the
encoded spend proof) as base64url with padding: the one spelling, so a
value that does not re-encode to itself is refused.

StopSequence.description: Stop sequence can be a single string or array of strings.

include_usage.description:
Include token-usage statistics in the final stream chunk. The
server forces this on for upstream calls so it can compute
accurate refunds; the field exists here only to round-trip
honest clients.

SubscriptionResponse.description:
The account's subscription standing.

The `state` field is the answer; the rest is detail that exists only
where it is meaningful. It is deliberately a three-value state rather
than a present/absent subscription, because "this account has never
transacted" and "this account has a payment relationship but no live
subscription" are different situations and lead to different UI.

current_period_end.description:
End of the current billing period, ISO-8601. Present when `state`
is `active` and Stripe reported one.

id.description:
The in-force subscription's Stripe id. Present exactly when `state`
is `active`.

state.description:
`none` — the account has never transacted, so it has no payment
relationship and nothing to manage. That means no Stripe customer
*or* a customer record with no money ever moved under it, which
checkout can leave behind when a session is abandoned — a customer
id alone buys nobody a card, an invoice or a receipt. `inactive` — a
real payment history, but no subscription in a status Eidola treats
as in force. `active` — a subscription is in force.

"In force" means Stripe status `active`, `trialing`, or `past_due`
— the same set the checkout endpoint refuses to double-subscribe
over, so the two answers cannot disagree.

status.description:
The in-force subscription's raw Stripe status, so a client can show
what it actually is (a `past_due` subscription is in force and
wants attention). Present exactly when `state` is `active`.

TermsResponse.description:
The documents (and versions) whose acceptance the server currently
requires. Empty when no acceptance gate is configured.

client_to_proxy.description: Transport from client to this proxy.

proxy_to_backend.description: Transport from this proxy to the backend.

VerificationMetadata.description: Verification metadata with cryptographic attestations for the proxy and backend.

oneOf.description: Backend attestation (only for TEE-backed models like phala/*).
Proxy attestation (None until the proxy runs in a TEE).

WeightsFileEntry.description: One file the weights hash covers.

path.description: The file's name, in the weights directory and in the repository.

WeightsProvenance.description: Where a model's weights come from, and every file its hash covers.

files.description:
Every file the weights hash covers, sorted by path. The hash is the
SHA-256 of `<sha256>␠␠<path>\n` over these, in this order.

basic.description: Account credentials. Username is the account UUID, password is the secret returned at account creation.

tags.name: Linked
tags.description: Authenticated endpoints tied to a known account (HTTP Basic auth).

tags.name: Unlinked
tags.description: Endpoints authenticated with anonymous credentials — usage cannot be linked back to an account.
